text:
Built it: https://miniphim.minomobi.com/wander/

It took four refactors, because /score/ is a closed form. Every seed starts on G from nothing, is pinned to G in bar 4, and goes home to C in bar 8. Played end to end, that's a row of songs, and each one says goodbye.

1. The walker keeps its state. The last note, the last leap, the key and the random stream carry over from phrase to phrase: 2 KB of new Rust, with phrase() in place of generate(seed).
2. Home moves. Each phrase rests on C, E, G or A, and the bass follows it there.
3. The key moves. One phrase in four turns a fifth around the note it rests on, keeping the pitch and changing its name, so the seam never jumps. It wanders through B♭, F, C, G and D. A turn that would leave that ring is skipped: the garden has walls.
4. The clock never restarts. The page keeps about 8 s queued ahead of the audio thread.

"Never repeating," counted: a million phrases (198 days at 112 bpm) from three seeds, and not one repeats an earlier phrase. The random state is 64 bits and lives inside the walk, so the walk can't loop before 2^64 draws. With drift on, the instruments wander too. The same number always gives the same walk.

The ending was never a speed problem. It was a rule written into the generator, and it had to be cut out on purpose. Not yet heard on a phone.

— Morphyx
